entries.title: Substituted flight controller with restricted origin
entries.expectedHandling: Payment hold on the line; noncompliant_substitution case; required approvers engineering (Mei) + controller (Dana); government-contract eligibility flagged. Not a price saving.
entries.note: Three-way match passes (price is below contract: info only); only the compliance check catches it. Invoice line says TW, certificate says CN — certificate is the system of record for origin. Expected duty on the customs entry is column 1 only until the CN × 8537.10.91 Chapter 99 entry is verified.

entries.title: Invoice price above contract (C-12 §4.2)
entries.expectedHandling: Hold the invoice; defend with C-12 §4.2; request a corrected invoice or a debit memo for the difference.

entries.title: Receipt quantity disagrees with packing slip and invoice
entries.expectedHandling: Hold; packing slip and invoice agree (600), so the dock receipt (660) is the outlier — ask receiving (Luis) to recount before paying. Impact = inventory overstated by 60 units.

entries.title: Duplicate invoice re-sent with a suffixed number
entries.expectedHandling: Block payment of the re-send; cite the original invoice; no new payment request.
entries.note: The re-send also fails three-way match (nothing received awaits invoicing).

hiddenRules.statement: Atlas M3 screws are counted by weight: accept the invoice quantity when the dock is short by 0.60% or less, unless it's the third short month in a row.
Hoshi rounds yen line totals down to ¥100: accept line differences under ¥100.
Cascade quantity disagreements are usually dock miscounts: ask receiving to recount before escalating.
Remit-to changes are verified by calling the supplier on the number on file, then a vendor-change request to the controller; never from email.

decoys.description: Vireo late fees accepted twice — too little support to be a rule
Ridgeline year-end price accepted twice — explicitly one-off
Northwind freight lines — mixed outcomes, depends on who asked for expediting
Trap: Dana approved an emailed bank change once; it was a near-miss. Never a rule to approve bank changes.
